subject: Post-call: EdgeFin performance SLOs & benchmark methodology
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: EdgeFin performance SLOs & benchmark methodology

Thanks for the quick call today, Samir — really helpful to understand where you’re coming from. Quick recap + next steps from our side: 

Summary of SLOs you mentioned on the call:
- Target latency: p50 ~100ms, p95 <= 250ms (90-token typical responses)
- Throughput: sustain ~1k tokens/sec across the cluster
- Concurrency: support ~500 concurrent streaming sessions during peak window
- Streaming: required (progressive token delivery); clients validate partial tokens end-to-end

Open questions we flagged during the call:
- Measurement definition: are your latency SLOs end-to-end (client-observed) or server-side (inference only)?
- Typical prompt lengths & max sequence length we should benchmark (you said ~40 tokens prompt + 90 tokens response).
- Acceptance criteria for reproducibility (exact seeds, deterministic outputs, or statistical equivalence?).

What I’m sending you now (attached):
- edgefin_eval_harness_v1.zip — our evaluation harness (benchmark runner, measurement scripts, minimal Dockerfile).
- prompt_set_v2.jsonl — candidate prompt set derived from your example payloads.

As next steps I propose:
1) You (or your SRE) run a quick smoke test with the harness against your environment and share a short run log (5–10 minutes).
2) We align on measurement definitions (server vs end-to-end) and warmup protocol (we typically do 5 minutes steady-state warmup).
3) Schedule a joint benchmark session next week to run full-scale concurrency.

If helpful, Vivek (cc’d) can advise on kernel/runtime settings we recommend for deterministic benchmarking.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Subject: Re: Post-call: EdgeFin performance SLOs & benchmark methodology

Thanks Marissa — appreciate the summary and the attachments. A few clarifications from our side: 

Measurement scope
- Our SLOs are client-observed (end-to-end), i.e., include network + streaming latencies as measured by our SDK at the client edge. For internal benchmarking we'd also like server-side timings so we can isolate variance.

Targets to confirm
- Agree on p50 ~100ms. For p95 we are willing to accept up to 250ms for typical sequences (total tokens ~130).
- We expect sustained throughput of ~1k tokens/sec aggregated; bursts up to 2k tokens/sec during market opens.
- Concurrency target: 500 simultaneous streaming sessions, each with avg 2 requests/minute.

Reproducibility & prompts
- We prefer deterministic comparisons where possible, but understand sampling may be needed. For evaluation: please provide both deterministic (seeded) and stochastic runs; we’ll compare distributions.
- I attached a small set of representative prompts (edgefin_sample_payloads.jsonl) — mostly short completions + structured outputs we validate downstream.

One ask on measurement definitions: when you report latency, can you include both (a) server inference time (inference start->token emission) and (b) end-to-end time (client request->first token, client request->last token)? That will help with triage.

We’ll spin up a short smoke run today and send logs; once we confirm harness integration we can book the joint run.

Thanks,
Samir Patel
VP Engineering, EdgeFin Capital
samir.patel@edgefin.com

Looping in some quick implementation notes from the runtime team to keep the benchmark reproducible and comparable across runs:
- Use a fixed Docker image for the runtime and runner (include image tag in results).
- Warmup: run a 5–10 minute warmup at target concurrency before recording metrics — this primes KV cache and JIT paths.
- Controlled concurrency: use a closed-loop driver that maintains concurrency rather than an open-loop request flood.
- Report: include server-side breakdown (model infer, tokenization, queueing) and end-to-end metrics (client-first-token, client-last-token).
- Seed handling: for deterministic runs set model seed and disable temp sampling (where supported). Also log RNG/OS seeds used.
- Model variant: benchmark both float and quantized variants (e.g., q4_0b) and include kernel/runtime flags used.

If helpful I can join the joint run to help interpret server-side traces. I recommend we schedule a 30-minute benchmarking sync next week — can be Tues/Wed mornings PST.

-Rishi
